drug_identity.off_label_note: All provided dosages for dogs and cats are extra-label.

metabolism_and_clearance.extra_information: Probenecid can reduce the renal tubular secretion of both ampicillin and sulbactam. Azotemic dogs show increased elimination half-life.

organ_burden_logic.note: Based on reported adverse effects and contraindications.

brain.evidence: High doses or increased CNS penetration associated with neurotoxicity (e.g., ataxia). Ampicillin lowers seizure threshold in humans.

blood.evidence: No significant primary hematologic burden; potential secondary risk with warfarin interaction.

kidney.evidence: Increased plasma ampicillin concentrations and elimination half-life in azotemic dogs; dosage adjustment may be needed.

liver.evidence: Elevated liver enzymes reported in some dogs. Contraindicated in humans with history of ampicillin/sulbactam-associated cholestatic jaundice.

heart.evidence: Tachycardia has been reported as an effect in dogs.

brain.evidence: High doses or increased CNS penetration can cause neurotoxicity.

kidney.evidence: Primarily renally cleared; high doses in renal disease may induce CNS effects.

liver.evidence: Hepatotoxicity reported in humans, veterinary significance unknown.

heart.evidence: No specific cardiovascular burden noted for cats.

timing_profile.evidence: Pharmacokinetic profile of parenterally administered sulbactam closely mirrors ampicillin in most species.

_ddi_note: Can cause false-positive urine glucose determinations when using cupric sulfate solution.

drug_interactions.evidence: Concurrent use implicated in increased occurrences of skin rashes in humans.
Beta-lactam antibiotics can inactivate aminoglycosides in vitro (and in vivo in chronic kidney disease).
Evidence of in vitro antagonism; use together generally not recommended but clinical importance unclear.
Concurrent use may increase risk for hypokalemia.
Ampicillin may decrease renal excretion of MTX, increasing concentrations and potential toxicity.
Concurrent use may reduce concentrations or effects of mycophenolate.
Reduces renal tubular secretion of ampicillin and sulbactam, maintaining higher systemic concentrations.
Concurrent use may decrease vitamin K production and increase risk for bleeding.

renal_dose_adjustment.note: Dosage adjustment (reduced dosing frequency) may be needed in azotemic dogs due to increased AUC and elimination half-life.

hepatic_dose_adjustment.note: Periodic liver panel recommended in patients with pre-existing hepatic dysfunction.

effects_and_mechanisms.common_mechanism: Ampicillin inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis. Sulbactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that broadens the spectrum by protecting ampicillin from hydrolysis.

species_notes.dog: Azotemic dogs may require reduced dosing frequency. High doses associated with ataxia. Elevated liver enzymes have been reported.
species_notes.cat: Useful for infections susceptible to amoxicillin/clavulanate when oral dosing is not viable.

dog.evidence: Use with caution in azotemic patients; neurotoxicity risk at high doses.

storage_and_forms.storage: Powder should be stored at temperatures at or below 30°C (86°F).
forms: Powder for injection (1.5 g, 3.0 g vials; 15 g bulk)

section_1_2_10.highlights: Parenteral potentiated aminopenicillin used when an injectable antibiotic is required. May be used for surgical prophylaxis. Hypersensitivity reactions possible. Usually administered SC, IM, or IV every 6 to 8 hours.
section_1_2_10.indications: Treatment of aerobic or anaerobic gram-positive and gram-negative infections when parenteral therapy is required. Considered when oral amoxicillin/clavulanate is not viable, or for surgical prophylaxis.
section_1_2_10.client_info: Because of the dosing intervals required, this drug is best administered to inpatients only.
